About us

Te Kaunihera-ā-rohe o Ngāmotu – New Plymouth District Council (NPDC) is shaping the future of our district. We’re here to serve our community and create a place where people love to live, work and visit. Guided by the principles of Te Tiriti o Waitangi, we’re committed to building strong partnerships that honour and celebrate our rich cultural heritage.

    We’re proud to share Destination Kāwaroa won the Beca Award for Excellence in Placemaking at last night’s LGFA Taituarā Local Government Excellence Awards!

    Taituarā — Local Government Professionals Aotearoa

    5,336 followers

    1mo

    Congratulations to the winners of the Beca Award for Excellence in Placemaking! New Plymouth District Council has taken out the award for Destination Kāwaroa – a partnership with Ngāti Te Whiti, the Taranaki Foundation and New Plymouth Partners that has transformed Kāwaroa Park into a vibrant, intergenerational destination on the city's foreshore. Co-designed with mana whenua and shaped by the community, the space brings together play, learning, accessibility and cultural storytelling, creating a place that celebrates the unique identity and history of Taranaki while welcoming thousands of visitors each day. The judges said Destination Kāwaroa was one of the clearest demonstrations of placemaking this year, with community engagement strongly reflected throughout the design and delivery of the project. Congratulations also goes to Horowhenua District Council, which received a Highly Commended award for Building a Sense of Place for Former Refugee Whānau in Horowhenua. Ka rawe to everyone involved in creating spaces that strengthen connection, belonging and community pride.

    People behind the play Ever wonder who keeps our playgrounds safe, clean and ready for action? Meet Kara Belcher - a powerhouse of our hard assets team which look after 49 playgrounds, nine skateparks and five basketball courts from New Plymouth to Ōākura and Ōkato - making sure they stay safe, clean and ready for fun. From monthly inspections and graffiti clean‑ups to topping up cushion fall (that woodchip that saves tamariki when gravity wins), Kara’s always on the move. Her biggest enemy? Rust. Coastal life keeps her team busy battling salty air, shifting wood and the occasional bit of vandalism - but community service requests help them jump on issues fast. And her favourite part of the job? Playground renewals. “I love it,” she says. “We review the designs, choose the best concept, and before you know it - boom - a brand‑new playground ready for our tamariki.” Kara’s work, alongside the wider Parks team, keeps our play spaces awesome. 🎉🌳🛝
